title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #17

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which part of a plant makes fruits and seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Root
   B. Stem
   C. Leaf
   D. Flower

2. Which of these shows a plant reproducing? (1 mark)
   A. A stem getting taller
   B. A leaf turning green
   C. A bean plant making pods with seeds
   D. A root drinking water

3. Why is it important to protect wild animals and their homes? (1 mark)
   A. They can be sold cheaply
   B. They are part of nature and bring visitors to Kenya
   C. They are dangerous to all people
   D. They do not need food

4. What is a vertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. An animal with six legs
   B. An animal that lives in water only
   C. An animal with a backbone
   D. An animal without bones

5. Frogs have smooth, wet skin and spend part of their life in water. They are (1 mark)
   A. Birds
   B. Mammals
   C. Reptiles
   D. Amphibians

6. What is bloating? (1 mark)
   A. A cut in the mouth
   B. A full, swollen tummy often with gas
   C. Loose faeces
   D. Tiredness

7. What does the rectum do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes saliva
   B. Stores faeces for a short time
   C. Chews food
   D. Digests proteins

8. A pupil has hard dry faeces. Which is the best advice? (1 mark)
   A. Eat only white bread
   B. Stop drinking water
   C. Eat more sweets
   D. Eat more fruits, vegetables and drink water

9. Which unit is used for the mass of a sack of maize? (1 mark)
   A. Litre
   B. Kilogram
   C. Second
   D. Metre

10. What does volume mean? (1 mark)
   A. How heavy it feels
   B. The amount of matter in an object
   C. The colour of an object
   D. The amount of space an object takes up

11. Why is air matter? (1 mark)
   A. It is invisible
   B. It is light
   C. It is cold
   D. It has mass and takes up space

12. Which of these is NOT matter? (1 mark)
   A. Milk
   B. Air
   C. Light from a torch
   D. A stone

13. What is decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Waste that rots and breaks down
   B. Waste made of plastic
   C. Waste made of metal
   D. Waste that never changes

14. What does reuse mean? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it away
   B. Bury it
   C. Burn it
   D. Use something again

15. Which waste goes into a compost pit? (1 mark)
   A. Tins
   B. Vegetable peelings
   C. Glass
   D. Plastic bags

16. What is a compost pit used for? (1 mark)
   A. Storing glass
   B. Storing plastic
   C. Turning kitchen waste into manure
   D. Burning waste

17. What should you wear when collecting waste? (1 mark)
   A. A hat only
   B. Nothing
   C. Sandals only
   D. Gloves and closed shoes

18. What is the best way to deal with metal scrap in a school? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it in a river
   B. Bury it in the school garden
   C. Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it
   D. Burn it

19. Which of these is non-decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Banana peel
   B. Leaves
   C. Egg shells
   D. Tin can

20. What is rainwater harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Drinking rainwater from puddles
   B. Selling rainwater
   C. Catching and storing rainwater
   D. Digging wells

21. Which of these reduces water use when brushing teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Using a cup of water
   B. Using a hose
   C. Leaving the tap running
   D. Using a bucket of water

22. What does water conservation mean? (1 mark)
   A. Selling water
   B. Using water carefully and protecting water sources
   C. Wasting water
   D. Boiling water

23. What is weight? (1 mark)
   A. The pull of gravity on an object
   B. The colour of an object
   C. The amount of light
   D. The heat of an object

24. A pump pushing air into a tyre is an example of (1 mark)
   A. A gas
   B. A colour
   C. A shadow
   D. A force

25. What effect is shown when a force starts a still football moving? (1 mark)
   A. Stops motion
   B. Changes shape only
   C. Starts motion
   D. Holds it together

26. A lighthouse is used to (1 mark)
   A. Warn ships of danger
   B. Cook food
   C. Grow plants
   D. Dry clothes

27. What is heat? (1 mark)
   A. A type of gas
   B. A form of energy that makes things hot
   C. A kind of sound
   D. A kind of matter

28. Why do farmers dry maize in the sun before storing it? (1 mark)
   A. So it becomes heavier
   B. So it becomes wetter
   C. So it starts to grow
   D. So it does not rot or grow mould

29. Which of these sources of heat uses electricity? (1 mark)
   A. Electric iron
   B. Firewood
   C. The sun
   D. Charcoal jiko

30. Which of these is unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Playing with matches
   B. Asking an adult to light a fire
   C. Switching off an iron
   D. Using gloves

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials. (3 marks)

32. Give three ways of saving water at home. (3 marks)

33. Explain what gravity is and give two examples of its effects. (3 marks)

34. Explain how gravity helps and how it can cause problems in daily life. (5 marks)

35. Describe the function of each part of the digestive system: mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. (5 marks)

36. Describe how animals respond to changes around them. Give four examples. (4 marks)

37. A bat has wings. Explain why it is not a bird. (3 marks)

38. Explain why plastic bags are a danger to the environment. (3 marks)

39. Give four ways in which heat is used in farming. (4 marks)

40. Explain why heat from the sun is important to the Earth. (3 marks)

41. State three ways of keeping teeth healthy. (3 marks)

42. Suggest two ways to make toys or ornaments from waste and the materials needed. (4 marks)

43. Describe an experiment to show that a solid keeps its shape but a liquid takes the shape of its container. State what you would observe. (5 marks)

44. State the difference between mass and volume. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Flower
   Flowers make fruits that contain seeds.

2. C — A bean plant making pods with seeds
   Making seeds is reproduction. Growing taller is growth.

3. B — They are part of nature and bring visitors to Kenya
   Wild animals are part of our environment and bring income through tourism.

4. C — An animal with a backbone
   Vertebrates have a backbone.

5. D — Amphibians
   These features describe amphibians.

6. B — A full, swollen tummy often with gas
   Bloating means the tummy feels full and swollen.

7. B — Stores faeces for a short time
   The rectum stores faeces before they pass out.

8. D — Eat more fruits, vegetables and drink water
   Fibre and water help soften faeces.

9. B — Kilogram
   Mass is measured in grams and kilograms.

10. D — The amount of space an object takes up
   Volume is the space a substance takes up.

11. D — It has mass and takes up space
   Air fills balloons and pushes against things, so it takes up space.

12. C — Light from a torch
   Light has no mass and takes up no space.

13. A — Waste that rots and breaks down
   Decomposable waste is broken down by decomposers.

14. D — Use something again
   To reuse is to use again.

15. B — Vegetable peelings
   Only decomposable waste is composted.

16. C — Turning kitchen waste into manure
   Decomposable waste rots into compost.

17. D — Gloves and closed shoes
   Gloves and shoes protect from cuts and germs.

18. C — Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it
   Metal can be recycled.

19. D — Tin can
   Metal does not rot easily.

20. C — Catching and storing rainwater
   Harvesting means collecting rainwater from roofs.

21. A — Using a cup of water
   A cup uses only a little water.

22. B — Using water carefully and protecting water sources
   Conservation means saving water and using it wisely.

23. A — The pull of gravity on an object
   Weight is the pull of gravity on a thing.

24. D — A force
   The pump pushes air by force.

25. C — Starts motion
   A push makes a still object move.

26. A — Warn ships of danger
   Lighthouses show ships where land or rocks are.

27. B — A form of energy that makes things hot
   Heat is a form of energy.

28. D — So it does not rot or grow mould
   Heat dries the grain and dry grain keeps longer.

29. A — Electric iron
   An electric iron uses electricity.

30. A — Playing with matches
   Matches can start fires.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Transparent materials let almost all light through. Translucent materials let some light through. Opaque materials do not let light through.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, use a cup or basin, fix leaks, use a bucket instead of a hose, reuse washing water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gravity is the force that pulls objects towards the Earth. It makes rain fall and makes a thrown ball come down.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each example.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: It keeps us on the ground, makes rain fall and water flow downhill. It can make objects fall and cause injuries and break things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for help and 2 marks for problems and 1 mark for a clear explanation.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Mouth: chews and adds saliva. Gullet: pushes food down. Stomach: churns with juices. Small intestine: finishes digestion and absorbs food. Large intestine: takes back water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: A goat lifts its head at noise, a snail pulls into its shell when touched, birds fly away from danger, animals seek shade in hot weather.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each of three examples.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bat has fur and feeds its young on milk. Birds have feathers and lay eggs. So a bat is a mammal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fur, 1 mark for milk, 1 mark for mammal.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: They stay for many years, block drains, harm animals that eat them and pollute land and water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drying grain and crops, hatching chicks, keeping chicks warm, cooking, controlling pests, drying fish.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: It warms the Earth so plants and animals can live, it dries things, and helps the water cycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Brush at least twice a day, limit sweets and sugary drinks, visit a dentist, use clean toothbrush or chewing stick.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: A toy car from a box and bottle tops. Beads from rolled paper. A flower vase from a tin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each toy and 1 mark for each list of materials.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use a stone and water. Put the stone in a cup and then in a bowl. It keeps its shape. Pour water in the cup and then into the bowl and its shape changes with the container. Conclusion: solids keep shape but liquids take the container's shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for stone in both containers, 1 mark for water in both, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and volume is the space it takes up.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct meaning.
